turns.text: Ozone and scorched rubber, sharp enough to sting behind the nose before eyes even find the source — six floors of stripped ladder rungs climbing into a thin bleed of red emergency light, most of the metal already gone to torch-cuts and old teeth marks.

the shaft threads dead center through forty stories of NekoCorp arcology, HVAC roar bleeding thin through sealed ducts to either side, red strip lighting the only illumination this deep since the last work crew stripped the rungs for resale. two floors up a service hatch hangs ajar on a broken latch, warm air sighing out of it — laundry-smell, machine oil, and underneath both, something colder: server exhaust, close enough to taste.

Claws find purchase in torch-cut gouges instead of rungs, climbing on memory of every other stripped shaft in this district — the hatch's warm laundry-smell pulls at something almost forgotten, softer than fur ever gets down here, but the server-exhaust thread underneath it is the one worth following.

the hatch opens on a gutted laundry room repurposed floor to ceiling — humming server racks stacked where dryers used to sit, a tangle of pirated fiber snaking out through a hole hacksawed in the wall. hunched at a cracked terminal in the corner, a thin shape scrolls the same glowing page over and over, page number climbing into the hundreds, never once looking up at the new draft of cold air let in through the hatch.

Ears flick toward the terminal's low blue glow but the rest of the body holds back at the hatch's lip — that hunched shape hasn't moved in longer than any of the fans have cycled, locked into whatever page keeps climbing, and a stillness that total reads wrong before it reads safe.

the terminal throws its pale light up under a face gone thin, whiskers unmoving, a voice half under the fan noise, worn down to habit more than complaint — page six says the last page was a promotional example, page six always says that, over and over, like the sentence itself forgot how to end. the screen never advances past six no matter how many times a paw that isn't there anymore reaches for the down key.

[ SETTINGS ]
  [ ] option 1
  [ ] option 2
  [ ] ... (pg 247)

Doesn't approach — some things a cat learns to leave exactly as found. Backs off the hatch's lip at an angle, tail low, following the fiber cable instead of the shape hunched over it, out toward wherever the wire actually goes.

the fiber runs taut along a conduit channel, out past the laundry room's far wall through a gap chewed wide by teeth years before tonight's, ending outside on an exposed ledge two floors up — city sprawling out beneath it in a wash of tower-light and rain-haze, a relay box bolted to the rail humming warm under a tarp gone brittle with age.

Presses flank against the relay box's warm casing, tail curling loose along the rail's edge, forty stories of open air below meaning nothing next to the specific, animal comfort of something warm that isn't hunting.

a patrol drone rounds the tower's curve on its low sweep, running light catching rain-mist first and the ledge second, downlight crawling along brittle tarp and rail both, in no special hurry — just close enough tonight that hurry might start mattering soon.
Flattens against the relay box's shadow side, breath gone shallow, betting the tarp's ragged edge throws enough dark to read as nothing worth a second pass.

the downlight drags across the tarp's edge, hesitates half a beat longer than routine allows, then slides on past toward the next ledge in its circuit — whatever decided nothing here needed escalating keeps that decision to itself, rotor-whine fading back into the general hum of forty stories going at once.

______
  /______\   <- relay box, tarp corner flapping
 ( -.-  )-'
  \____/

Waits out three full breaths before moving again, then noses along the rail for whatever else the wind's carrying — under the ozone and rain there's a thread of scorched fur, old and half-gone, the specific burnt-metal smell that only comes off a cat who makes a habit of biting things that fight back.

the scorch-trail threads back toward the tower's service side, past a stretch of exposed rebar where a demolition notice still hangs peeling off one wall — whoever left that smell didn't come this way for the view, and the rebar's got fresh claw-gouges in it that don't match anything currently on this ledge.

Doesn't follow it — somebody else's grudge, somebody else's night. Turns back along the conduit channel instead, toward the shaft and whatever's left of the climb down before the sky starts going grey at the edges.

the shaft swallows the climb back down same as it swallowed the one up, red emergency light thinning toward the lower floors where the ladder rungs still exist in mostly one piece. forty stories up, the relay box keeps its private hum going under a tarp nobody's replaced in years, and behind a laundry-room hatch two floors up from that, a page number that was already impossible keeps climbing toward a seven it may never actually reach.

Finds the shaft's lowest landing, concrete cool and plain under damp paws, and folds down against the wall's angle — the scorched-fur thread gone, the terminal's blue glow gone, just the ordinary red bleed of emergency light and legs finally willing to stop.

the tower holds its forty floors of humming machinery same as it does every night, laundry-smell and server-exhaust both filtering down through a shaft nobody logged as accessible anymore, and low at the bottom of it, one small shape breathes even and slow, unbothered, unbilled, filed under nothing worth a second look.
